### What problem does this PR solve? <!--add issue link with summary if exists-->

This PR solves #12748 

### What is changed and how it works?

By creating a `nullableBool` type, we allow user to use `enable-xx` while keep `disable-xx` still valid. Due to the limitation of the implementation of `Config.Load` which overrides the caller, we can't distinguish user's option with the default ones, however using `nullableBool` to replace `bool` enables us to know what the user has put in the configuration file.

### Check List <!--REMOVE the items that are not applicable-->

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

 - Unit test
 - Integration test

Code changes

 - Has exported variable/fields change

Side effects

 - Increased code complexity

Related changes

 - Need to update the documentation

Release note

Deprecated `disable-timestamp` and `disable-error-stack` for log configuration, introduce `enable-timestamp` and `enable-error-stack` for replacement.

review_comments: Miss the test of unmarshaling from text to toml

We can use `defer` here, in case some error happens before `f.Close` and `os.Remove`.

```go
defer func() {
    f.Close()
    os.Remove(f.Name())
}()
```

I suppose we should keep the file if some error happens so that we could look into the file to double check since this part of code is for test purpose. This piece of code is borrowed from previous code in `TestConfig`, which did not use `defer` neither.

It'd be better use defer here to make the testing environment clean. TiDB has hundreds of contributors who may run the test but only few of them need to keep the file to do investigation. 
When you need double check you can delete the `os.Remove` code and rerun.

The file is not deleted only if some test is broken, in this case manual inspection is needed (although it is not likely to be broken if the code is not changed), and you could/should manually delete that file, or rerun the test which will delete it if not thing went wrong. I agree it make sense to use defer here, I will change it if you insist.

Do not test the data marshaling from the struct `nullableBool`, it will never happen in real world.
Here's a real-world test.
```go
data := []byte("true")
json.Unmarshal(data, &nb)
```
That's for the `map[string]interface{}` branch in UnmarshalJSON, I added more real world tests in the new patch.
Do we need `getEnableTimestamp` which maybe more intuitive?

Nope, in the internal logic we only need one option, and it is enough to have `getDisableTimestamp`. Historically we only have `DisableTimestamp`, so I created this mock function to provide a proxy for the added `EnableTimestamp` option.
History can be changed by your hands.

The internal logic is designed to support `Disable-xx`, of course I could make them all `Enable-xx` but I'm not sure about the consequences. 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/29735669/67670633-4bee1d00-f9af-11e9-95f7-b9b9fc3f92ec.png)

If you insist on this, I could make another PR to fix this.
The internal logic is not uniform. I think use `enable-xx` is more intuitive.
